# 2 Samuel Chapter 10 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 178v–179r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_010_page_001.jpg, 2SA_010_page_002.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** After this, the king of the Ammonites died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.

**2** David said, "I will show covenant-faithfulness to Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father showed covenant-faithfulness to me." So David sent his servants to comfort him concerning his father. And David's servants came to the land of the Ammonites.

**3** But the princes of the Ammonites said to Hanun their lord, "Do you think David is honoring your father because he has sent comforters to you? Has not David sent his servants to you to search the city and spy it out and overthrow it?"

**4** So Hanun seized David's servants and shaved off half of their beards and cut off their garments at the hips, and sent them away.

**5** When David was told, he sent to meet them, for the men were greatly humiliated. The king said, "Remain at Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then return."

**6** When the Ammonites saw that they had made themselves odious to David, the Ammonites sent and hired the Arameans of Beth-rehob and the Arameans of Zobah — twenty thousand foot soldiers — and the king of Maacah with a thousand men, and the men of Tob — twelve thousand men.

**7** When David heard of it, he sent Joab and all the army, the mighty men.

**8** The Ammonites came out and drew up in battle formation at the entrance of the gate, while the Arameans of Zobah and Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were by themselves in the open field.

**9** When Joab saw that the battle was set against him both in front and in the rear, he chose some of the best men of Israel and arrayed them against the Arameans. **10** The rest of the forces he placed under the command of Abishai his brother, and he arrayed them against the Ammonites.

**11** He said, "If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you shall come to my aid; and if the Ammonites are too strong for you, then I will come to save you. **12** Be strong, and let us be courageous for our people and for the cities of our God, and the LORD will do what is good in his eyes."

**13** Then Joab and the forces with him advanced against the Arameans, and they fled before him. **14** When the Ammonites saw that the Arameans had fled, they too fled before Abishai and entered the city. Then Joab returned from fighting against the Ammonites and came to Jerusalem.

**15** When the Arameans saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they gathered together. **16** Hadadezer sent and brought out the Arameans who were beyond the River Euphrates, and they came to Helam, with Shobach the commander of Hadadezer's army at their head.

**17** When David was told, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and came to Helam. The Arameans arrayed themselves against David and fought with him. **18** The Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed of the Arameans seven hundred chariot teams and forty thousand horsemen, and struck down Shobach the commander of their army, who died there.

**19** When all the kings who were servants of Hadadezer saw that they had been defeated by Israel, they made peace with Israel and became subject to them. And the Arameans were afraid to help the Ammonites anymore.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

All three translators agree on the narrative arc: diplomatic insult (vv.1-5), mercenary alliance (v.6), Joab's two-front battle strategy (vv.7-14), and the wider Aramean war resolved at Helam (vv.15-19). The *chesed* link to chapter 9 is consistently recognized. The key theological moment — Joab's speech in vv.11-12 — is handled similarly by all three, with the main variation being register. The numerical discrepancy with 1 Chronicles 19:18 is noted by all translators.

---
## Disagreement Log

### V.2 — "covenant-faithfulness" vs. "faithful love"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "covenant-faithfulness"
- **PNEUMA:** "faithful love"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "covenant-faithfulness" — per project convention; maintaining continuity with chapter 9.

### V.3 — "princes" vs. "commanders"
- **EMET:** "princes [sarey]"
- **LOGOS:** "princes"
- **PNEUMA:** "commanders"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "princes" — *sarey* can mean princes, officials, or commanders. In a royal court addressing the king, "princes" fits the diplomatic context.

### V.4 — "buttocks" vs. "hips" vs. "waist"
- **EMET:** "up-to their-buttocks [ad shitoteyhem]"
- **LOGOS:** "at their hips"
- **PNEUMA:** "at the waist"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "at the hips" — *shitoteyhem* refers to the buttocks/hips region. "Hips" (LOGOS) preserves the meaning without unnecessary crudeness or euphemism.

### V.5 — "ashamed" vs. "humiliated"
- **EMET:** "exceedingly ashamed [niklamim]"
- **LOGOS:** "greatly humiliated"
- **PNEUMA:** "too humiliated to come home"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "greatly humiliated" — *niklamim* means shamed/humiliated. PNEUMA's addition "to come home" adds interpretation not in the text.

### V.6 — "become odious" vs. "made a stench"
- **EMET:** "they-had-become-odious [hiv'ishu]"
- **LOGOS:** "made themselves odious"
- **PNEUMA:** "made a stench of themselves"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "made themselves odious" — captures *hiv'ishu* without PNEUMA's colloquialism.

### V.7 — "mighty men" vs. "elite warriors"
- **EMET:** "the-mighty-men [gibborim]"
- **LOGOS:** "the mighty men"
- **PNEUMA:** "the elite warriors"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "the mighty men" — *gibborim* is rendered consistently as "mighty men" per project convention.

### V.9 — "chosen ones of Israel" vs. "best men" vs. "best fighters"
- **EMET:** "all [the]-chosen-ones of-Yisra'el"
- **LOGOS:** "some of the best men of Israel"
- **PNEUMA:** "the best fighters in Israel"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "some of the best men of Israel" — *mibchar* = chosen/select. LOGOS balances precision and readability.

### V.12 — "let us be strong" vs. "let us be courageous" vs. "let's fight with everything"
- **EMET:** "let-us-be-strong [nitchazaq]"
- **LOGOS:** "let us be courageous"
- **PNEUMA:** "let's fight with everything we have"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "let us be courageous" — *nitchazaq* (hithpael of חזק) means "let us strengthen ourselves/be courageous." LOGOS's rendering is most fitting for a military speech. PNEUMA paraphrases too freely.

### V.12 — "will do the good in his eyes" vs. "what he sees as right"
- **EMET:** "will-do the-good [ha-tov] in-his-eyes"
- **LOGOS:** "will do what is good in his eyes"
- **PNEUMA:** "will do what he sees as right"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "will do what is good in his eyes" — preserves the Hebrew idiom *ha-tov be-einav*. PNEUMA's "right" narrows the meaning; *tov* = good, not merely right.

### V.18 — "seven hundred chariots" (numerical discrepancy)
- **EMET:** "seven-hundred chariots" (notes 1 Chr variant)
- **LOGOS:** "seven hundred chariot teams" (follows MT, notes variant)
- **PNEUMA:** "seven hundred Aramean chariots"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "seven hundred chariot teams" — LOGOS's "chariot teams" clarifies that *rekev* refers to chariot units, not individual vehicles. The 1 Chronicles variant (7,000) is noted but not adopted.

---
*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
